in_text_mentions: An onion-skin lesion is concentric fibrosis around the bile duct epithelium (Fig. 5A) [29]. In the 2024 diagnostic criteria, onion-skin lesions are limited to those associated with degeneration or the disappearance of bile duct epithelium. Fibrous obliterative cholangitis is fibrous occlusion of the bile duct lumen caused by the progression of an onion-skin lesion (Fig. 5B) [30]. Both onion-skin lesions and fibrous obliterative cholangitis are characteristic, but not specific, findings of PSC in liver biopsies, as similar findings are seen in hepatolithiasis [31]. A: MR cholangiographic patient image showing multiple short, band-like biliary strictures, a characteristic structural manifestation of PSC. B: MR cholangiographic patient image demonstrating the characteristic beaded appearance produced by alternating short annular strictures and relatively normal or minimally dilated ducts in PSC. C: MR cholangiographic patient image shows narrowing, reduced arborization, and peripheral pruning of the intrahepatic ducts, explicitly identified as the characteristic PSC pruned-tree appearance. D: MR cholangiographic patient image shows diverticulum-like outpouching between adjacent biliary strictures, a characteristic structural finding presented by the disease-focused caption for PSC.
